assertions.label: Fresh positively verified private core starts empty
Exact nonce sentinel belongs to the verified private core
Full sentinel generation and QA ownership verified
Private app uses the original verified core generation
No native layout/mod errors
Exactly the seven required Mission Control mods are installed from fresh builds, each passed herdr-app check, and both layout files and previews are byte-identical to the bundle sources
The second host is a separate positively owned private core reached only through a controlled via transport, not a real remote machine
Classic starts terminal-first under one topmost Mission Control tab bar with its work panel hidden
Settings and Add machine sit at the bottom-left of the 220 px rail and open Herdr’s own Settings and machine dialogs
The bar’s panel control opens the Classic work panel on its first source
The Classic panel draws all six local source icons inside the panel
In Classic, Jira, GitHub issues, pull requests, GitLab issues, merge requests and previous sessions each show only their own view without a repeated heading
A pinned GitLab issue start in the Classic panel runs the chosen tool in a workspace-plus-issue worktree created from the focused linked checkout
The issue agent tab is named automatically with its issue key and task title
Repeating the same pinned start focuses the existing issue agent instead of starting another
A real tab-menu rename gives the issue agent tab the person’s manual name
One swap click switches Classic to Mission Control keeping the selected space and tab, every tab, running terminal address and manual name
Mission Control restores the source selected in Classic (GitLab issues)
In Mission Control the six navigation sources each show only their own view without a repeated heading
Jira, GitHub and GitLab issue views are compact boards grouped into To do, In progress and Done
An All-spaces GitLab issue sharing its provider ID with another account starts only on its own host, repository, project and account
An All-spaces Jira issue sharing its key and ID with another account starts only in its own space, repository and account
A pinned GitHub issue start runs the third pinned tool from the focused linked checkout
A Mission Control merge-request review reaches its pinned tool from the focused linked checkout with the opaque MR identity
Closing the renamed agent through the tab menu and Reopen last agent resumes its exact session once in its original folder
The person’s manual name returns once on the reopened agent tab
Previous sessions resumes an exact saved session in its own checkout on this Mac
Previous sessions in All spaces includes the second host’s history with its host label
Right-clicking another space opens that space’s own menu, including Previous sessions, without changing the selected space
New agent from that menu starts in the right-clicked space’s repository on its own machine
The private world holds 128 spaces and native rail search reaches and selects the 128th
A space without a repository shows no other repository’s issues
The Agents section lists dozens of agents from both hosts
Agent rows show exact session context and shared-account quota as separate readings
Agent rows draw the actual tool icon beside each task name
The Priority and Spaces quick actions regroup the agents list
One swap click switches Mission Control back to Classic keeping the selected space and tab, running terminal addresses and manual names
Classic restores the source selected in Mission Control (merge requests)
A held All-spaces merge-request action keeps its captured host, project and account through space and scope changes
With the second host offline its spaces read offline and its actions start nothing, while a local action still starts
The second host’s spaces return after its transport reconnects
At 736 px Classic keeps the swap, all six panel sources and the bottom-left footer reachable without clipping
At 736 px beside the 220 px rail all six sources show whole short labels and a short-label source can be selected
At 736 px the bottom-left Add machine control still opens Herdr’s machine dialog
At 1024 px beside the 220 px rail all six sources show whole full labels and remain selectable
At 1024 px the Classic panel’s six sources remain drawn and selectable
Swaps at 736 and 1024 px keep the selected space and tab, terminal addresses and manual names
No observed native text shows mojibake or replacement characters
Both layouts with all seven mods produced zero native app errors
Every owned provider request was read-only and carried only its own account’s synthetic fixture credentials
Scenario used real native input and captured a native frame

boundary: Task-owned GPUI app/core with PID-bound native input. Existing instances were not queried. Provider authentication is not proven.
